## 1. Goal

Compile the same `core/` to WebAssembly with flat exported functions the website can call, plus a headless Node runner so CI can compare WebAssembly output with the console program. This settles O-10 (where the error lives when `aprm_create` fails).

## 2. Background

**From PRD §5 WebAssembly exports:**

Flat functions, so JavaScript never builds C structs. Each returns a status, or a pointer to a JSON string owned by the simulation and valid until the next call on the same handle.

| Export | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `aprm_create(cpu, mem, policy, alpha_milli, T, eps)` | Returns a handle (≥ 1) or a negative error. `api.c` sets `max_jobs` to the website limit (5,000) |
| `aprm_add_job(h, id, arrival, duration, cpu, mem, priority)` | Adds one job; returns a status |
| `aprm_step(h)` / `aprm_run_until(h, t)` | Advance the simulation |
| `aprm_state(h)` / `aprm_log(h, since)` / `aprm_results(h)` / `aprm_metrics(h)` | JSON strings |
| `aprm_last_error(h)` | JSON error envelope for the last failed call |
| `aprm_exact(h)` | Runs the exact solver on the handle's jobs (n ≤ 9) |
| `aprm_reset(h)` / `aprm_destroy(h)` | Clear or free |

**From PRD §3 Emscripten flags:**

**Emscripten flags (in `wasm/build.sh`).** Modular output with a named factory, single-file output (WebAssembly embedded in the JavaScript), memory growth allowed, and only the step API functions exported. Exact flag spellings are checked against the current Emscripten documentation when the script is written.

**From PRD §9 CI baseline (build-wasm):**

4. **build-wasm:** install the frozen emsdk version, `make wasm`.

**From DECISIONS D26, D27, O-10:**

| # | Decision | Reason | Rejected alternatives | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D26 | WebAssembly exports are flat functions taking numbers and returning a status or a JSON string owned by the handle | JavaScript never builds C structs | Passing structs across the boundary | PRD §5 |
| D27 | `max_jobs` is a field of `SimConfig`: the console program sets 1,000,000, `wasm/api.c` sets 5,000 | The core must know its own limit to return `LIMIT_REACHED` | A compile-time flag per build; an unchecked limit | R1 |

| # | Question | Why it matters | Decide in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| O-10 | Where `aprm_last_error` finds the error when `aprm_create` fails (no handle yet) | WebAssembly API | K-13 |

## 3. Scope

**In scope:**

- Flat exports in `wasm/api.c` wrapping the step API with a handle table (handles ≥ 1)
- `max_jobs` = `APRM_MAX_JOBS_WEB` (5,000) set in `api.c`
- Per-handle last-error storage and the O-10 decision for create failures
- `wasm/build.sh`: modular output with a named factory, single file, memory growth, only the step API exported
- `wasm/run_wasm.mjs`: reads a jobs CSV and policy flags, prints `results.csv` to stdout
- CI job build-wasm

**Out of scope:**

- Website JavaScript (K-23)
- `aprm_exact` body (K-33; export returns an error until then)
- Conformance at scale (K-21)
- Freezing the emsdk version (K-18)

## 5. Specification

Exports (PRD §5): `aprm_create(cpu, mem, policy, alpha_milli, T, eps)` → handle ≥ 1 or negative error; `aprm_add_job(h, id, arrival, duration, cpu, mem, priority)`; `aprm_step(h)`; `aprm_run_until(h, t)`; `aprm_state(h)`, `aprm_log(h, since)`, `aprm_results(h)`, `aprm_metrics(h)` → pointer to a JSON string owned by the handle, valid until the next call on the same handle; `aprm_last_error(h)` → JSON error envelope; `aprm_exact(h)`; `aprm_reset(h)`; `aprm_destroy(h)`.

Numbers cross the boundary as JavaScript numbers; `api.c` range-checks every value (safe integers up to 2^53) before converting to `int64_t`. The handle table is the only mutable global and lives in `wasm/`, never in `core/`.

`build.sh` flag spellings must be checked against the current Emscripten documentation when written (PRD §3); the output file is `web/vendor/aprm.js` (git-ignored, D47). `run_wasm.mjs` usage: `node wasm/run_wasm.mjs --policy fcfs --in jobs.csv` → `results.csv` text on stdout, exit codes as the CLI.

## 9. How to verify

```sh
make wasm
node wasm/run_wasm.mjs --policy fcfs --in tests/cases/fcfs_basic.csv > /tmp/w.csv
build/aprm --policy fcfs --in tests/cases/fcfs_basic.csv --out /tmp/c.csv
cmp /tmp/w.csv /tmp/c.csv
```
A pass: `cmp` prints nothing.

## 10. Viva notes

**Idea:** the website calls the exact same C code, compiled once more; flat number-only functions mean JavaScript never builds C structs.
**Examiner question:** "Is the website really running your C code?" — Yes, compiled to WebAssembly, and the conformance test checks identical output on 1,000 cases.

## 11. Pitfalls

- Using flag names from memory (check the docs)
- Returning a pointer that a later call overwrites while JS still reads it
- Large integers above 2^53 losing precision
- Forgetting to export memory helpers needed to read C strings (`UTF8ToString`)
- `aprm_run_until(h, t)` does not move the clock to `t`: `now` stays at the last event handled (D59), so the state JSON's time can be less than `t`
